bug_description.original: A use-of-uninitialized-value vulnerability exists in the encodeCodepoint() function.
bug_description.normalized: When ArduinoJson parses the exact 7-byte witness `'\\uDDe?`, `JsonDeserializer::parseVariant()` consumes the opening single quote and routes into the quoted-string path. `JsonDeserializer::parseQuotedString()` then allocates local `Utf16::Codepoint codepoint` with no constructor, so `codepoint._highSurrogate` is indeterminate. The escape selector `u` sends control to `parseHex4()`, which decodes `DDe?` into UTF-16 code unit `0xDDEF` because vulnerable `decodeHex()` treats `?` as nibble `0x0f`. `Utf16::Codepoint::append()` recognizes that code unit as a low surrogate and computes `_codepoint = 0x10000 + ((_highSurrogate << 10) | (codeunit & 0x3FF))` before `_highSurrogate` has ever been written. `parseQuotedString()` then forwards `codepoint.value()` to `Utf8::encodeCodepoint()`, and MemorySanitizer reports the first observed use at the `codepoint16 < 0x20` branch in `Utf8.hpp:26`. The patch fixes this by adding `Codepoint() : _highSurrogate(0) {}`.

source.description: First project-level consumer on the vulnerable path. `parseVariant()` reads byte `0x27` from the staged witness, dispatches to the quoted-string case, and with `filter.allowValue()` true routes control into `parseStringValue()` / `parseQuotedString()`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is the exact 7-byte sequence `27 5c 75 44 44 65 3f` (`'\\uDDe?`). This statement consumes the leading byte `0x27` (`'`) as the dispatch key that selects quoted-string parsing.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: MSAN crash site. `encodeCodepoint()` branches on `codepoint16`, which is derived from the poisoned `codepoint32` value built from the uninitialized `_highSurrogate` state.
sink.note: Both `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` name `src/ArduinoJson/Json/Utf8.hpp:26:9` in `Utf8::encodeCodepoint()` as the observed `use-of-uninitialized-value` location.

root_cause.description: This stack allocation instantiates `Utf16::Codepoint` without a constructor in the vulnerable revision, so `codepoint._highSurrogate` starts indeterminate until some earlier high-surrogate append writes it.
root_cause.note: The patch fixes this state origin by adding `Codepoint() : _highSurrogate(0) {}` in `src/ArduinoJson/Json/Utf16.hpp`.

tainted_value_origin.description: MSAN attributes the poison to allocation of local `codepoint` in `parseQuotedString()`'s stack frame at line 357; the concrete vulnerable object is this line-359 declaration, whose `_highSurrogate` member is left uninitialized in the vulnerable revision.

parser_admitted.description: After the leading `0x27` selects the quoted-string cases, `filter.allowValue()` is true on the saved reproducing call chain, so control enters `parseStringValue()` and then `parseQuotedString()`.

fine_trace.note: Source. `parseVariant()` reads the leading witness byte `0x27` and dispatches through the quoted-string case. On the saved reproducing path `filter.allowValue()` is true, so control reaches `parseStringValue(variant)` for the attacker-controlled buffer.

Root-cause state origin. Entering quoted-string parsing allocates local `codepoint` on the stack, but the vulnerable `Utf16::Codepoint` type has no constructor, so `_highSurrogate` is still uninitialized at this point. MSAN's origin frame points to this stack allocation in `parseQuotedString()`.

Inside the escape branch opened by witness byte `0x5c`, the next attacker-controlled byte is `0x75` (`u`), so the parser chooses Unicode-escape decoding instead of ordinary `EscapeSequence::unescapeChar(c)` handling.

Across four iterations, `parseHex4()` accumulates bytes `D`, `D`, `e`, `?` into `result == 0xDDEF`; vulnerable `decodeHex()` treats `?` as `0x0f` because it subtracts `'0'` for any character `< 'A'`. The caller's `codeunit` is therefore a lone low surrogate.
The parsed `codeunit` `0xDDEF` falls in the low-surrogate range `0xDC00..0xDFFF`, so `append()` takes the branch that expects `_highSurrogate` to already contain a previous high-surrogate payload.

This formula reads `_highSurrogate` before any write has occurred on the witness path, combines it with `codeunit & 0x3FF`, and stores the resulting poisoned `_codepoint`. MSAN names this line as the site where the uninitialized value was stored to memory.

On this low-surrogate path line 389's `if (codepoint.append(codeunit))` condition is true, so `parseQuotedString()` immediately forwards `codepoint.value()` from the same `Utf16::Codepoint` object into `Utf8::encodeCodepoint()`.
Inside the sink function, the poisoned `codepoint32` from step 7 is shifted and truncated into local `codepoint16`, which is the value immediately tested at the crash site.
MSAN sink. Reading `codepoint16` at this branch is the first observed use of the poisoned value, matching `sanitizer_trace.txt` and `reproduction_report.json` at `Utf8.hpp:26:9`.

allocation_context.note: MSAN says the uninitialized value was created by allocation of `codepoint` in this stack frame; the concrete local declaration is `Utf16::Codepoint codepoint;` at line 359.

sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch adds `Codepoint() : _highSurrogate(0) {}` in `src/ArduinoJson/Json/Utf16.hpp`, which removes the exact uninitialized `_highSurrogate` state consumed in fine-trace step 6.

cross_validation.sink_matches_crash: Yes. Fine-trace step 9 is the exact `Utf8::encodeCodepoint()` branch at `Utf8.hpp:26` named by both the saved MSAN report and `reproduction_report.json`.
cross_validation.root_cause_matches_allocation_context: Yes. MSAN attributes the poison to allocation of local `codepoint` in `parseQuotedString()`'s stack frame, and the rebuilt root-cause step 2 is the concrete line-359 declaration that creates that uninitialized object state before step 6 reads `_highSurrogate`.
cross_validation.trace_consistent_with_stack: Yes. The saved stack `encodeCodepoint -> parseQuotedString -> parseStringValue -> parseVariant -> parse -> deserialize -> deserializeJson -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput` matches the coarse trace and the fine-trace handoff from steps 7-9 back through source step 1.
cross_validation.tainted_value_reaches_sink: Yes. Source step 1 routes the exact witness into quoted-string parsing, step 4 materializes `codeunit == 0xDDEF`, step 6 stores poisoned `_codepoint`, step 7 forwards `codepoint.value()` into `encodeCodepoint()`, and steps 8-9 show the reported sink consuming it.

format.name: Exact 7-byte single-quoted Unicode escape
format.contract: The verified trigger is the exact 7-byte file staged at `poc`: `27 5c 75 44 44 65 3f` (`'\\uDDe?`). Byte `0x27` selects the quoted-string path, bytes `5c 75` force the `\\u` Unicode-escape path, and `parseHex4()` decodes `44 44 65 3f` as `0xDDEF` because vulnerable `decodeHex()` maps `?` to nibble `0x0f`. That lone low surrogate is the first code unit appended to the uninitialized local `Utf16::Codepoint`, so `_highSurrogate` is read before initialization and the poisoned result reaches `Utf8::encodeCodepoint()`. No broader input class is claimed here.
